subject: Hosting evidence & action plan — mapping HIPAA/SOC2 needs to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@healthsync.io>, HealthSync Procurement <procurement@healthsync.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Hosting evidence & action plan — mapping HIPAA/SOC2 needs to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Maya / HealthSync team,

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation and helpful context on your data flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can converge on the right deployment mode.

Recap from our call:
- Primary requirement: processing PHI for clinical summarization; HIPAA compliance + signed BAA is mandatory.
- Security gating: SOC 2 Type II report requested for vendor approval; redacted report acceptable for initial assessment.
- Architectural preference: open to Hosted API if isolation + BAA + SOC2 evidence suffice, otherwise Dedicated capacity or Private VPC for stronger isolation and on-prem flexibility.
- Audit expectations: vendor to provide artifact package (SOC2, KMS details, log retention, network diagrams) and point-of-contact for audit support.

What I need from HealthSync to finalize recommendation:
1) Estimated steady-state token throughput and concurrent requests (typical peak QPS).
2) Number of patient records touched per month and data residency preference.
3) Whether HealthSync requires on-prem deployment (air-gapped) or if VPC-hosted private deployment is acceptable.

What Redwood can provide (next actions we propose):
- We will share a redacted SOC 2 Type II and our standard BAA template for procurement review.
- For Hosted: list of additional controls we can enable (customer keying via KMS, private inference keys, audit logs with configurable retention).
- For Dedicated/Private: architecture checklist and timeline estimate (Dedicated: reserved capacity on our managed infra; Private: VPC or on-prem package + install window).

Attachments: redwood-hosting-options-onepager.pdf (brief on differences & expected timelines).

Proposed next steps:
- HealthSync to confirm answers to the three items above by EOD Thu 11/12.
- Redwood to circulate SOC2 redacted bundle and BAA draft by EOD Fri 11/08.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to go through options and pick a preferred path.

Thanks — I’m looping Marissa (CS) and Aditya (AM) so they can prep the deployment and commercial side.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: Hosting evidence & action plan — mapping HIPAA/SOC2 needs to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Thanks Rishi — good summary. A few clarifying points from our security and procurement teams: 

- HIPAA/BAA: absolutely required. Procurement will only engage with vendors where a signed BAA is possible and the vendor can commit to our minimum data retention and deletion SLAs.
- SOC2: we need the Type II report for the most recent 12-month period; redacted copy is acceptable for initial review but procurement will want confirmation we can access the unredacted version under an NDA during contract review.
- Audit: we run annual vendor audits and occasionally ad-hoc requests. Do you support on-demand audit evidence within 30 days?
- Deployment preference: we'd prefer Hosted API if you can guarantee logical isolation and customer-managed keys. However, if that cannot be reconciled with our procurement requirements we will evaluate Dedicated or Private.

I’m attaching our security intake (short) and a note from procurement describing the approval gating criteria.

Can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood supports KMS integration for customer-managed keys across Hosted and Dedicated; 2) what logs/retention are available for audit (API logs, access logs, admin audit trail) and the retention windows we can configure?

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call.

— Maya
Maya Patel | Head of Platform Security, HealthSync
maya.patel@healthsync.io

Attachments: HealthSync_security_overview.docx (1 doc)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@healthsync.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosting evidence & action plan — mapping HIPAA/SOC2 needs to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Maya — I’m Mina from Redwood’s Security & Compliance team. Thanks for the clear asks. Short answers + attachments we can share immediately.

1) KMS / customer-managed keys:
- Hosted: we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for encrypting data at rest; tokenization and inference keys can be scoped per-customer.
- Dedicated: same KMS integration; you also get network isolation and can pair with customer VPC peering.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): we support BYOK and HSM integrations for on-prem installs — we will provide guidance during architecture review.

2) Available logs and retention:
- API request/response audit logs (redacted request bodies on hosted unless requested), admin activity audit trail, billing/usage logs.
- Default retention: 90 days. Configurable up to 24 months on Dedicated/Private with retention controls.
- For audit: we can provide filtered exports and a read-only access window for auditors.

3) SOC2 / BAA / audit support:
- Attached: SOC2-2025-redacted.pdf (redacted Type II report) and BAA_draft_Redwood_v1.pdf (our standard BAA).
- We can provide the unredacted SOC 2 under NDA for procurement review and support on-demand audit evidence; our standard SLA for on-demand artifact delivery is 14 days, though we’ll commit to 30 days for this engagement if needed.
- For deeper audits (control-level walkthroughs), we schedule 2–4 weeks in advance — we’ll provide POA&M and architecture docs in advance.

4) Quick recommendation based on your stated constraints:
- If you can accept Hosted + customer-managed KMS + signed BAA + redacted SOC2 review, we can enable extra isolation controls and on-boarding is fastest (2–3 weeks).
- If procurement insists on unredacted SOC2 on day 0 or stricter network isolation, Dedicated is recommended (4–6 weeks to Reserve + onboard).
- For full on-prem or air-gapped requirement, Private deployment is possible but requires a multi-week install and security review (6–12 weeks).

I’ve also attached a short checklist for Private deployment (Private-deploy-checklist.xlsx) showing required artifacts and timelines. I’ll make myself available to join any procurement calls.

— Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: SOC2-2025-redacted.pdf, BAA_draft_Redwood_v1.pdf, Private-deploy-checklist.xlsx
